label: CONNECTION

cover.headline: Staying *a team* through the holidays
cover.sub: 5 ways to keep the season from pulling you apart.

points.heading: Plan the hard parts together
points.body: Talk about the tricky visit or the long drive before it happens, not in the car on the way.
points.panel: “Which part of this week are you dreading most?”

points.heading: Agree on a signal
points.body: A small sign means “I need a break” without a scene in front of family.
points.panel: Pick a word or a touch on the arm that means “let’s step outside.”

points.heading: Back each other up in public
points.body: Disagree later, in private. In the room, you’re on the same side.
points.panel: “We’ll talk it over and get back to you.”

points.heading: Keep one moment just for you two
points.body: A short walk or a quiet coffee before the house wakes up.
points.panel: “Can we sneak out for ten minutes, just us?”

points.heading: Debrief kindly afterward
points.body: Share what went well before what didn’t. The season is long.

close.save: Save this before the first family visit.

caption:
The holidays can bring a marriage closer or quietly wear it down, often in the same week.

A little planning helps. Not a strategy for winning the season, just a few ways to keep feeling like teammates while everything else gets busy. Pick one or two that fit your family, and talk them over before the first visit.

Share this with someone who’s hosting this year, and follow @spotseason for more.
